newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.95 pct in correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.95 pct in correction.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended early gains in continued reaction buys on Tuesday afternoon, recouping Monday's losses with the help minor liquidity influx, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,433, up 41 points, or 2.95 percent from Monday when it dived 2.73 percent on political uneasiness as well as poor inflation data and first quarter company results.
Daily trade volume rose to 11.05 trillion lira ($81 million) from Monday's 9,81 trillion ($72 million).
"Turnover is still weak, so we cannot say that an upward move has started. Today's rise may remain as a short-lived correction," said Okan Alpay from Interbank.
Some brokers said low sale in a Treasury bond auction might have helped to spur the afternoon purchases because of expectations of excess liquidity to be left in the money market on Wednesday.

The Treasury sold 34.6 trillion lira of two-year inflation-indexed bonds at 25 percent risk premium. Banks will pay 34.3 trillion lira for the auction on Wednesday when the Treasury will inject 130 trillion lira for bond redemptions.
The market had dived 6.6 percent between April 24 and May 2 on concerns over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition government after the market opened following a 6-1/2 day holiday.
